items.title: Motorcycle Exports H1 FY2027 – Boxer, Star City, Pulsar, CT, FZ, Apache, Gixxer, Raider, Xtreme
items.summary: India’s motorcycle exports grew 31.83% during April–September 2026, with Boxer and Star City together contributing nearly 46% of overseas shipments.
items.text: India’s motorcycle exports reached 27,64,662 units in the first half of FY2027, up 31.83% from 20,97,158 units in April–September 2025. Overseas shipments increased by 6,67,504 units, driven primarily by substantial gains for Bajaj Boxer and TVS Star City. Total two-wheeler exports stood at 32,07,357 units in H1 FY2027, growing 31.86% over 24,32,412 units. Motorcycles contributed 86.20% of shipments. Scooter exports expanded faster at 34.95% to 4,35,363 units, accounting for 13.57% of the total. Moped exports declined 42.03% to 7,332 units, contributing the remaining 0.23%. Bajaj Boxer retained the top position with 6,68,804 units, growing 90.56% over 3,50,972 units a year earlier. Its increase of 3,17,832 units was the largest among the ranked motorcycle families, taking its share of motorcycle exports to 24.19%. TVS Star City followed with 6,01,720 units, up 46.06% from 4,11,961 units. It added 1,89,759 units and accounted for 21.76% of shipments. Together, Boxer and Star City contributed 45.95% of motorcycle exports . Their combined increase of 5,07,591 units represented approximately 76% of the segment’s net export growth. Bajaj Pulsar ranked third with 3,01,449 units, up 17.26%, while CT followed with 2,15,040 units, growing 31.89%. The top four entries collectively accounted for 64.63% of motorcycle exports. items.title: Ducati Monster V2 Dark unveiled, India launch in 2027
items.summary: The Monster V2 Dark minimises theatricality while stripping the Monster down to its dark essentials, with no mechanical changes.
items.text: Ducati has launched the Monster V2 Dark in global markets, priced at EUR 10,990 (or Rs. 11.69 lakh). The Monster was launched in August 2026, the next chapter in the Monster model's storied history. The Monster V2 Dark will serve as the entry-level model, losing out on a few key features while also offering a minimalist, yet sinister blacked-out design. The Monster was Ducati's first street naked motorcycle, launched in 1992. Since then, the Monster has gone through multiple iterations while retaining its core ethos of simplicity and accessibility. The Monster V2 Dark takes a step further, offering the Monster V2 in a proverbially stripped-down variant, finished in Ducati Dark livery. The aesthetic differences go beyond skin-deep, too. Underneath the jet-black bodywork, Ducati has left the frame, exhaust endcaps, and intake snorkel unpainted, contrasting against the black paintwork. The rims are now all-black, losing out on the red highlights found on the standard model. The seat has been changed slightly too, with a uniform choice of material throughout the seat; the Monster Dark also loses out on the rear seat cowl that buyers would normally get as standard equipment. Interestingly, the Monster Dark also loses out on the LED sequential turn indicators from the standard bike, while the Ducati Quick Shift (DQS) bi-directional quickshifter has become an optional accessory. The latter uses a Benelli-sourced parallel-twin engine, whereas the X350 T is expected to use a downsized version of the single-cylinder engine from the X440 T. While the X440 T uses a 440cc, single-cylinder motor, the Harley-Davidson X350 T is expected to be powered by a 349cc motor. This will allow Harley-Davidson to position it in the sub-350cc category, which attracts 18 per cent GST compared to the 40 per cent applicable on the X 440T. items.title: SHAD Unveils Terra Crash Bars for BMW R 1300 GS
items.summary: SHAD is expanding its Terra adventure range into motorcycle protection with upper and lower crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS. Possible India availability after EICMA 2026.
items.text: SHAD Terra crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS are set to make their show debut at EICMA 2026. This is an important expansion of the Spanish accessory maker’s adventure-focused Terra range. Until now Terra has largely been associated with panniers, top boxes and soft luggage. The addition of motorcycle protection takes the range into a new category and SHAD has chosen one of the most established large adventure motorcycles as its first application. There’s two separate protection systems for the BMW R 1300 GS. Upper Crash Bars are designed to protect the fuel tank, radiator and upper bodywork. The Lower Crash Bars concentrate on the engine, crankcase or oil sump area and exhaust headers. This modular arrangement is useful because owners can choose the degree of protection they need. Although the upper bars require the corresponding lower crash bars to be installed first. Both assemblies are made from AISI 304 stainless steel. SHAD uses 25mm-diameter tubing with a 2mm wall thickness, with the structure designed to provide high strength without adding unnecessary width around the motorcycle. The bars mount directly to the R 1300 GS ’ existing chassis mounting points, meaning installation does not require cutting or drilling the motorcycle. You can pick between two finishes. Indian is now being separated from the shared corporate systems it previously relied on while under Polaris requiring the motorcycle company to establish its own finance, administration and operational teams. Indian Motorcycle has recently added engine production to the plant while also expanding its paint operations. It will help recruit up to 60 additional manufacturing employees as these capabilities grow. The expansion follows the C6’s rollout in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Flying Flea currently operates 12 sales and service centres in Bengaluru and another four in Hyderabad. With Pune adding 10 more, the company now has 26 touchpoints across its first three Indian cities. Royal Enfield says each Pune dealer is equipped to provide both routine maintenance and dedicated technical support. Pune city has a sizeable two-wheeler population, a strong technology and automotive industry presence and a large base of riders already familiar with premium motorcycles. items.title: Updated KTM 200 Duke Launched in India at Rs. 2.07 Lakh
items.summary: The updated KTM 200 Duke has been launched in India at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom). The motorcycle has received some new features, including a traction control system, a bi-directional quick shifter, among others. Here’s a detailed breakdown:
items.text: KTM has updated the 200 Duke in India, and the bike has received some substantial updates. The updated bike is now priced at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom); this makes it Rs. 1,552 more expensive. It now comes with a new ride-by-wire throttle, unlocking some new features alongside tweaks to its underpinnings. On the features front, the bike now gets two riding modes: Street and Rain, likely to alter the throttle response. In addition, the brand has added a traction control system for better safety. An interesting bit taken from the higher-capacity 390 Duke is the crawl feature. This is a low-speed assist that prevents the bike from stalling at lower speeds, and should make city rides a lot easier. Lastly, for spirited riding, the Duke now gets a bidirectional quickshifter for clutchless up- and downshifts. The underpinnings have been revised, with the bike now getting a 43mm inverted fork and a fatter 150-section rear tyre. This is a welcome change, as the brand had updated the bike earlier with a smaller 37mm WP Apex fork and a thinner 140-section tyre, which felt like a slight downgrade . Apart from the features and underpinning changes, the bike now comes with two additional colours: Liquid-carbon and a full black shade. Aside from these, the bike remains mechanically unchanged. It continues to be powered by the same 199.5cc, single-cylinder, liquid-cooled motor producing 24.67bhp and 19.3Nm.

items.text: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has proposed allowing motorists to exceed prescribed speed limits by up to 20 percent before being issued speeding challans on expressways. The suggestion could effectively raise the enforcement threshold to 144 km/hr on stretches where the maximum permitted speed is 120 km/hr. Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on Highways of India’s Future, Gadkari said he had instructed officials not to issue notices to motorists travelling at speeds of up to 120 km/hr. He added that a 20 percent margin could be considered beyond the prescribed limit, with challans issued for violations exceeding that threshold. If implemented on expressways with a 120 km/hr speed limit, the proposed margin would translate into an enforcement threshold of 144 km/hr. However, the proposal does not amount to an increase in the legal speed limit. Motorists are still required to adhere to the posted speed restrictions, and any change in enforcement policy would need to be formally communicated by the authorities. Reports suggest a smaller version of the X440T’s engine, but final displacement remains unannounced. Government guidance sets GST at 18% for motorcycles up to and including 350cc, compared with 40% above 350cc. That gives the downsizing speculation a clear pricing context. The X350T photographed in India should be distinguished from the X350 sold in China. BikeWale identifies the Chinese bike as a QJ-linked parallel-twin model. Harley’s own parts catalogue records its 353cc engine and Chinese manufacture; the Indian X350T is reported to follow the X440T platform. The spy-shot reports do not include an official price or a confirmed India launch date. BikeWale suggests a possible EICMA 2026 appearance. events.text: India Bike Week is coming back for 2026, and the details about the event have been released. Just like last year, it is being hosted in Panchgani, Maharashtra on 4 and 5 December, 2026. Motorsport is also a major part of IBW, and there are five different race events taking place this year spread across dirt, off-road, and closed course. Each one of them requires interested participants to register for them separately, and the IBW entry registration doesn’t cover it. Besides races, IBW 2026 will also offer its attendees a good mix of stunt shows, custom build exhibition, and live music. And just like every year, there could be new two-wheeler launches, but the exact models will be known closer to the event dates. Riding gear stalls will also occupy a big part of the event venue, offering riders a close look at new products from different brands and, perhaps, exciting offers on purchases. The pygmy hog was believed to be extinct by the mid-20th century. In Assam, the Pygmy Hog Conservation Programme was launched in 1995. A year later, six pygmy hogs were taken out of Assam’s grasslands to Manas National Park. Conservationists feared that their dwindling numbers could lead to extinction if they were not bred in captivity. The pygmy hog depends significantly on dense grasslands to feed. However, with the burning of grasslands and their conversion into tea estates brought down their numbers. Since 1996, there has been a 32-fold increase in the numbers of pygmy hogs. Since 2020, six groups of pygmy hogs have been released into the Manas National Park. The campaign addresses a common road safety concern: riders carrying helmets without wearing them. accessories.summary: The KTM 200 Duke is expected to cost around Rs 2.09 lakh (ex-showroom), with the latest version adding electronic rider aids and a new-looking black finish.
accessories.text: The KTM 200 Duke is expected to cost around Rs 2.09 lakh (ex-showroom), with the latest version adding electronic rider aids and a new-looking black finish. KTM is preparing another update for the 200 Duke in India, with the revised motorcycle already spotted at dealerships before its official launch. The changes focus on technology and rider assistance, bringing equipment previously associated with larger Duke models to the 200cc streetfighter. The company has yet to confirm the final specifications and pricing. The biggest addition is a bi-directional quickshifter, which allows riders to shift up and down through the gears without operating the clutch. The motorcycle also gets a ride-by-wire throttle, replacing the conventional mechanical throttle connection with an electronic system. This enables two riding modes: Rain and Street. The updated model is also expected to feature traction control, with a corresponding indicator visible on the 5-inch TFT instrument cluster. However, cruise control is not included. KTM has revised the right-side switchgear, giving it a design similar to the unit used on the 390 Duke. The left-side switchgear appears unchanged. The updated motorcycle is expected to retain its 199.5cc, single-cylinder, liquid-cooled petrol engine. It produces 25bhp and 19.3Nm of torque, with a six-speed gearbox transmitting power to the rear wheel. India Has Some Incredible Off-Road Motorcycling. Honda Wants In
accessories.summary: Honda is considering motocross and enduro bikes for India, where incredible terrain and a growing off-road scene await.
accessories.text: India is one of those places that should be on every adventure rider's bucket list. We're talking towering mountains, rocky trails, muddy forests, and enough challenging terrain to keep even the most experienced dirt bike enthusiasts thoroughly entertained. And while the country has no shortage of motorcycles, there's still plenty of room for more machines designed to tackle the rough stuff. Apparently, Honda has been paying attention. Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India is considering expanding its off-road lineup with dedicated motocross and enduro bikes. Company president and CEO Tsutsumu Otani confirmed that the brand is evaluating both categories, potentially opening the door to some seriously interesting machinery. Nothing's confirmed just yet, but it's a promising development for a market with enormous off-road potential. Honda already sells the XR300L and XR300 Rally in India, giving riders a couple of legitimate options for getting dirty. But its global off-road portfolio goes much further, from the beginner-friendly CRF50F to the competition-ready CRF450R. There are also street-legal options like the CRF300L and CRF300 Rally , which could make plenty of sense for riders who want to hit the trails without needing a pickup truck to get there. accessories.text: Classic Legends has taken a big step toward making motorcycle ownership completely hassle-free. They are setting up an authorized distribution network across India to supply genuine spare parts beyond their standard dealership network. This move directly addresses one of the primary expectations of motorcycle owners—getting timely and reliable access to original parts. By expanding availability to independent workshops, local service partners, and customers across urban, semi-urban, and emerging markets, the company aims to speed up part procurement, enhance spare parts availability, and drastically reduce service turnaround times nationwide. Commenting on the launch of the distribution network, Mr. Anupam Thareja, Co-founder of Classic Legends , stated: “As more riders choose Jawa, Yezdi and BSA, delivering a seamless ownership experience remains a key priority for us. Easy access to genuine spare parts is an important aspect of that experience and expanding our authorised distribution network is an important step towards making them more accessible across India. We have consistently listened to customer feedback and invested in strengthening our ownership ecosystem, with a focus on making support more accessible and convenient for our riders.
